solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: M, Alfie, ET and Surf's Up, say?

definitions.text: M, Alfie, ET and Surf's Up, say?

indicators.note: 's up reads as 'is up', stirred up or disturbed, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the apostrophe-s belongs to the indicator

explanation.surface: A list of four movie titles offered as examples.
explanation.walkthrough: The four titles are real films (Fritz Lang's M, the Michael Caine Alfie, Spielberg's ET, the animated Surf's Up), and their letters, with 'Surf's' read as 'Surf is', are stirred up to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Each title is a full-length movie made for cinema release, the standard industry term for the main programme film.

clue.text: Exhausted nurse, drained, receiving payment

indicators.note: something receiving an item takes it in, so one piece is placed inside the other words

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: A worn-out nurse, emptied of energy, finally gets paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The nurse and the word for drained sit side by side, and the payment goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfeebled means made weak, a close synonym of exhausted in the sense of drained of strength.

clue.text: Appearing topless after casual shirt becomes full of creatures?

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a T-shirt is casual wear, shortened to its letter

explanation.surface: Someone going topless after taking off a casual shirt, swarming with bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' looks like a state of undress but trims the head off the word for appearing; the question mark flags the definition as one specific use.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means swarming or abounding, as a pond is with living things.

clue.text: Line by storyteller written up

indicators.note: in a down entry, writing something upwards means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a liar tells stories, in the sense of untruths

explanation.surface: A line of prose penned by a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' sounds like an author, but here it means someone who tells fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a bar or track, and railway lines are made of rails.

clue.text: Following guide, hear about carved decoration

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Listening to a tour guide talk about a piece of carving.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation f. (as in 'pp. 10f.') joins the two words and all ten letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead is the carved bust or figure on the bow of a sailing ship, an ornament.

clue.text: Spooner noticed stolen goods in case

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds are exchanged

parts.note: noticed is saw and stolen goods is loot; say the pair with their opening sounds exchanged

explanation.surface: Spooner spots stolen goods hidden in a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of SAW LOOT and you get LAW SUIT. 'Case' looks like luggage, but it is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a case brought before a court, the legal sense of case.

clue.text: Proceed immediately enveloped in loose guernsey

indicators.note: something enveloped lies wrapped inside, so the letters sit within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Getting on with things right away while wrapped in a baggy fisherman's jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: A guernsey is a thick knitted wool sweater from the Channel Island of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move without pause from one piece or topic into the next.

clue.text: Reasonably cleverly made knickknack

parts.note: a pretty piece of work is one skilfully done

explanation.surface: A small ornament that has been crafted fairly skilfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word serves both senses in turn, one as an adverb, one as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists pretty-pretty as a noun for a small, over-ornamented trinket.

clue.text: Battering an assortment of food in capital of Greece

parts.note: a buffet is a spread of assorted dishes

indicators.note: 'capital of' keeps only the first letter of 'Greece'

parts.note: the capital, or initial letter, of the word Greece

explanation.surface: Food coated in batter, served as a spread in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Greece' looks like Athens, but it means the opening capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffeting is a repeated striking, as by wind or waves, much like battering.

clue.text: This may indicate a late sherry got drunk after opening of brandy!

definitions.text: This may indicate a late sherry got drunk after opening of brandy!

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
a drunk person staggers about, so these letters are put in a disordered order

explanation.surface: A police device revealing that a nightcap of sherry, after some brandy, has gone to someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: the device would show the drinking it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathalyser is the roadside device that measures alcohol on the breath of a driver.

clue.text: Bet on turning over joker first

indicators.note: first tells us which piece goes at the front of the build

parts.note: a wag is a jokey person

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Placing a bet on a card game where the joker is turned up first.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Latin-derived 'on the matter of', is turned around and the joker goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a bet, a stake placed on an outcome.

clue.text: Drug I encountered within clubs — it makes me sick

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A clubber who took a pill at a nightclub and now feels ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's order is loose: the drug comes first, then the meeting, then I, with clubs closing the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting, so the speaker is the thing that makes you sick.

clue.text: Barney's posh, married in white

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the colour word

parts.note: argent is silver or white in heraldry
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A posh wedding with everything in white.
explanation.walkthrough: A barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel. Argent is the heraldic name for silver, drawn as white.
explanation.definitionFit: A barney is an informal word for a row or dispute, which an argument is.

clue.text: Flyer written by two writers named George

wordplay.note: George Sand, the French novelist, and George R. R. Martin, author of the Game of Thrones books

explanation.surface: A book or leaflet produced by two authors who share a first name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a pamphlet written by them, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand martin is a small brown swallow-like bird that nests in sandy riverbanks.

clue.text: Great help for a change to give advance notice

indicators.note: a change means something is altered, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Being told ahead of time is a welcome help for once.
explanation.walkthrough: To telegraph a move, as a boxer telegraphs a punch, is to reveal it before it comes.
explanation.definitionFit: To telegraph is to signal one's intention in advance, without meaning to.

clue.text: Lacking in taste, like gum

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tasteless, cheap and vulgar
second meaning: sticky, as glue is

explanation.surface: Chewing gum that is both cheap-looking and bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taste' suggests flavour, but it is about style.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky means both vulgar or tawdry and slightly sticky to the touch, like wet paint or glue.

clue.text: Maybe learn about health club with Conservative minister

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round another piece
maybe suggests a possible version, so the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a gym is a fitness club

explanation.surface: A Tory government minister signs up at a gym to learn something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political next to 'Conservative', but here it means a church minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is an ordained priest or minister of the church.

clue.text: One who helps marauders edges away

indicators.note: with its edges taken away, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A helper watches as plunderers slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' reads like creeping off, but it strips the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aider is a person who gives help or assistance, a helper.

clue.text: Upset German teetotaller in Alcoholics Anonymous meeting

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down entry the word is turned upwards

parts.note: Ger. is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: in places the teetotal abbreviation inside the pair of letters

explanation.surface: A German non-drinker distressed at an Alcoholics Anonymous gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, one who drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting or event for boat races, as in Henley.

clue.text: A confused answer after doctor comes to

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A patient wakes up muddled and mumbles a reply after the doctor arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes to' suggests waking after fainting, but it means approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw near is to approach, as one comes to a place.

clue.text: Actor George touring North East African country

indicators.note: someone touring goes round a region, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: George Segal, the American film actor

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actor on tour in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation on the west coast of Africa, capital Dakar.

clue.text: Perhaps artist Ray in his early years?

definitions.text: Perhaps artist Ray in his early years?

parts.words: artist Ray in his early years
parts.note: surface reading: the painter Man Ray when he was a boy
setter's reading: any youthful male, with the artist's first name paired to an adjective for youth

explanation.surface: A biography of the surrealist photographer Man Ray as a youth.
explanation.walkthrough: Man Ray was the American surrealist artist; picture him young and his first name is all that is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A youthful male, like the artist Man Ray in youth, is a lad or youngster.

clue.text: Seize American lawman, say

indicators.note: say asks us to go by what is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Wyatt Earp, the Wild West marshal

explanation.surface: A US sheriff grabs something, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to take power or position by force or without right.

clue.text: Think about capturing German soldier

indicators.note: capturing holds a prisoner inside, so one piece goes within the others
about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reflecting on the capture of a German soldier in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: A knight was a mounted soldier in medieval times.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight was a medieval armoured soldier, serving a lord on horseback.

clue.text: Send up enthusiastic singer

indicators.note: sending up a word in a down entry runs it from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Mocking an over-eager vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' looks like mockery, but it reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Belch leads to ravening, unpleasant creature appearing in Alien

indicators.note: appearing in places those letters inside the following word
the leads of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A hungry, nasty monster bursts out in the film Alien with a burp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' recalls the film with the monster, but it stands for ET.
explanation.definitionFit: To eruct is a formal or literary verb meaning to burp.

clue.text: Lean on sticky, unknown object

explanation.surface: Resting against something tacky whose identity is a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean on' reads as a verb phrase, but lean is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingummy is a placeholder word for an item whose name you can't recall.

clue.text: Arrange journey by sea around island — it's easy

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word is wrapped round a letter

explanation.surface: Organising a cruise round an island is smooth going.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain sailing is an idiom for a task that proceeds smoothly with no difficulty.
